title: Can Deterministic Network Verification Reduce Undetected Faults in LLM‑Generated Configurations?
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study id c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) to measure whether inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM intent→configuration generator and an emulated execution reduces the proportion of configurations that would execute with operational faults. Using shared_initial_candidate semantics (one identical LLM candidate per intent evaluated both without and with verification), we evaluated 72 preregistered paired intents with gpt-5-mini and a canonical deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution completed with 144 episodes (72 pairs) and 72 model calls. All baseline executions produced no emulator-observed faults (n_11 = 72, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0). The paired difference in undetected-fault proportion is 0.0 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics this degenerate confirmatory outcome is expected when identical generated candidates produce no baseline execution faults. We provide preregistration rationale, deterministic execution accounting, representative validator traces, exact inferential outputs, and artifact-grounded methodological recommendations for future experiments that can reveal verifier utility under realistic error regimes.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intents into device-level configurations for network operations (NetOps). This intent→configuration translation can accelerate change pipelines but risks silent reachability, policy, or ordering violations when generated device commands are executed. A common mitigation is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) architecture pairing stochastic generation with deterministic verification and—optionally—repair or human review. Prior work documents intent→configuration prototypes and GVR-style proposals [1–3], yet systematic, preregistered experiments that couple LLM outputs, canonical verifiers, and executed end-to-end emulator outcomes are limited.

We preregistered study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 to isolate a narrow but consequential question: when an identical generated candidate for an intent is evaluated both without and with a deterministic verifier (shared_initial_candidate semantics), does the verifier materially reduce the proportion of configurations that execute with operational faults? This paired design isolates pure detection ability on the same candidate and avoids confounding from generator sampling variability. We report a completed confirmatory run (72 paired intents) with artifact-grounded accounting and a degenerate ceiling/null outcome (zero baseline faults). Rather than treating that outcome as a null endorsement of verifiers, we analyze why it arose under the preregistered contract and provide concrete, artifact-supported guidance for future confirmatory designs that can measure practical verifier utility.
sections.related_work: LLM-driven intent→configuration work has shown promising task-level accuracy in constrained settings [1]. Prototype co-pilots and multi-agent frameworks have integrated validators to reduce regressions, but public evaluations often lack preregistered detection tests against executed outcomes [2,4]. The generate–verify–repair pattern is established in code-generation and software-repair literature where deterministic checks and test suites validate stochastic outputs [3]; adapting these architectures to network semantics motivates experiments that quantify verifier true- and false‑positive behavior relative to actual execution faults. Classical deterministic network verification (header‑space and policy checkers) provides precise invariants (reachability, ACL effects, ordering) and is a natural verifier candidate for GVR stacks [5]. Our study positions a rigorously preregistered paired detection test within this literature and clarifies its narrow estimand under shared_initial_candidate semantics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. The study preregistration (c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) froze the design and analysis prior to execution. The primary estimand is the paired reduction in undetected operational-fault proportion: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The confirmatory hypothesis H1 targeted an absolute paired reduction of 0.20 with two-sided alpha = 0.05 and power ≥ 0.80; the preregistered sample size was N = 72 pairs stratified equally across three topology/difficulty strata (24 pairs per stratum).

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract. Per the execution_contract, each intent produced exactly one initial LLM generation shared across the two paired conditions. Baseline: the shared candidate is executed in an isolated emulator and the outcome (fault/no fault) is recorded. Guarded: the canonical deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) runs on the same candidate; if the verifier flags violations the guarded outcome is recorded as prevented (no emulator execution); if not, the identical candidate is executed. Under these semantics the verifier cannot alter the generated candidate distribution—its only possible effect on the paired estimand is detection and prevention of violations on the shared candidate.

Model, adapter, and verifier configuration. The archived model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json) declares requested_model = "gpt-5-mini" and provider = "openai_responses"; runtime sampling used the provider default (temperature recorded as null in the archived configuration). The adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1; verifier id is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = "5.0") implementing full_intent_constraint_validation and producing structured validator_trace outputs including parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, validation_before/after states, violation_codes, and difficulty metadata.

Task-bank generation, contamination controls, and stratification. Tasks were generated deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Each task manifest entry encodes a natural-language intent, an expected final state, a required_sequence (the command ordering required for safety), allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty label (medium/hard/very_hard). The preregistered sampling plan stratified the confirmatory sample equally across three difficulty strata (24 pairs per stratum). Deterministic exact-match contamination checks were applied against public corpora per preregistration; any exact-match would have produced exclusion from confirmatory analysis. No confirmatory pairs were excluded in the executed run.

Execution protocol, retries, and deterministic accounting. The missingness_plan allowed up to two additional retries for transient hosted-API errors. The execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 144, completed_episode_count = 144, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 72 (one shared generation per pair). Deterministic_reconciliation.json reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 72 and cache_miss_count = 72, with stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 72}, consistent with the shared_initial_candidate contract and one generation per intent.

Scoring and inferential procedures. The verifier yields episode-level binary validity (valid vs violation) plus structured traces. The primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 to build the 2×2 paired contingency table and apply an exact McNemar two-sided test when discordant pairs exist. We computed paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence intervals for the paired difference with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap seed = 1729) to provide reproducible uncertainty quantification. Pre-specified subgroup confirmatory tests (topology complexity and policy type) were registered; Holm correction was reserved for these comparisons.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting. The run completed without technical failures. Deterministic artifact counts: planned_episode_count = 144, completed_episode_count = 144, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 72. Provider-call accounting in deterministic_reconciliation.json shows completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 72 and cache_miss_count = 72, consistent with one shared generation per pair.

Paired contingency and inferential outcomes. Aggregating the 72 confirmatory pairs yields counts guarded×baseline: n_11 = 72, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. The paired estimate paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.0]. Per-condition summaries (analysis/condition_summary.csv) record baseline success_rate = 1.0 and guarded success_rate = 1.0. The archived analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) contain the exact CSVs and bootstrap parameters.

Representative validator traces and command statistics. Representative scoring artifacts for six example pairs are archived under execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json through task-000006-*.json. Across these representative traces parsed_command_count ranges 2–6 and required_command_count ranges 2–6; observed_touched_field_count values in examples range 2–4. Each example shows validator_version = "5.0" and violation_count = 0. The representative traces also include normalized_configuration, validation_before and validation_after final_state mappings, and difficulty.level entries (medium/hard/very_hard). These artifacts confirm the verifier executed its deterministic checks and produced no violation flags for the sampled candidates.

Contamination, missingness, and exclusions. analysis/contamination_summary.csv reports zero exact-match contaminations for confirmatory pairs. analysis/missingness_summary.csv records complete_pairs = 72 and zero failed or unscorable episodes. No preregistered exclusions were applied, simplifying interpretation but producing a ceiling effect that eliminates the possibility of observing verifier benefit under this paired contract.

Sensitivity checks. Pre-specified sensitivity analyses (treating excluded pairs as failures; bootstrap diagnostics) were run against the archived artifacts. Because there were no excluded pairs and no discordant outcomes these sensitivity analyses reproduce the degenerate numerical conclusion (paired difference = 0.0). The bootstrap setup (seed = 1729, resamples = 10000) is recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl and reproduces the reported CI collapse to a point mass.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the ceiling outcome. The paired shared_initial_candidate design validly isolates verifier detection on identical candidates. Observing zero baseline faults yields a scientifically informative ceiling/null outcome: under the chosen model (gpt-5-mini), prompt/template, and synthetic task bank the generator outputs were uniformly valid in the emulator and thus the verifier had no executed failures to prevent. The contingency counts (n_11 = 72, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0), p = 1.0, and bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0] are direct consequences of the preregistered contract and observed data rather than evidence that deterministic verification is unnecessary in general.

Design implications for future confirmatory studies. The shared_initial_candidate contract is methodologically clean but insensitive to verifier-mediated improvements that require altering the executed candidate distribution. To measure practical verifier utility, future preregistered confirmatory designs should include one or more of: (1) independent-generation arms permitting separate generator calls per condition so that verifier-triggered repairs or sampling differences can change executed candidates; (2) repair-enabled flows where the verifier, upon flagging, triggers a single deterministic repair call and the repaired candidate is executed and assessed end-to-end; (3) adversarial or fault-injection task banks intentionally seeded to increase baseline error prevalence (sequencing violations, ambiguous intents, protocol‑edge cases) to reveal true positive/false positive tradeoffs; (4) multi-model and sampling-parameter sweeps to quantify model- and sampling-sensitivity to verification performance.

Threats to validity and artifact-grounded limitations. Internal validity: the one-shared-generation per intent and provider-default sampling (temperature = null in execution/model_configuration.json) introduce runtime sampling semantics that were recorded but not experimentally varied. Construct validity: emulator-observed faults are a conservative proxy for operational harm but do not capture traffic-dependent, timing, or cross-device emergent failures present in production hardware. External validity: the experiment used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), a synthetic/emulated task bank, and one deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Conclusion validity: because baseline error prevalence was zero for the preregistered task bank the confirmatory design lacked power to demonstrate verifier benefit for this execution. Residual risks: deterministic provenance and exact-match checks were applied, but private model-training contamination cannot be fully ruled out and remains residual uncertainty.

Operational implications. The absence of baseline emulator faults in this constrained, emulated setting indicates that modern LLMs can produce high task-level accuracy under narrow prompts, dialect restrictions, and deterministic task generators. Organizations should nevertheless treat deterministic verifiers as a layered control. Demonstrating concrete verifier utility for operational risk reduction requires experiments deliberately designed to produce measurable baseline error rates or to permit verifier-mediated candidate changes (independent generation or repair flows).
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired evaluation (study id c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to test whether a canonical deterministic verifier reduces the proportion of LLM-generated configurations that would execute with operational faults. For the chosen model (gpt-5-mini), verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and synthetic/emulated task bank, baseline executions produced zero emulator faults and the verifier did not change outcomes (paired difference = 0.0, bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], exact McNemar p = 1.0). This artifact-grounded null/ceiling outcome is internally consistent with the preregistered design: when identical generated candidates produce no executed faults, a verifier cannot reduce executed faults under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Measuring verifier utility under realistic error regimes requires experimental contracts that permit independent or multiple generator samples, repair-enabled flows, adversarial task sets, and multi-model comparisons. All execution artifacts, validator traces, and analysis logs referenced here are archived in the evidence bundle to support replication and focused follow-on studies.

Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and approved the immutable initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the lock. Models and tools: initial generation used gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version recorded in execution/model_configuration.json) orchestrated via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = "5.0") served as the canonical verifier; an isolated emulator executed candidate configurations. Preregistration: study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 was preregistered and frozen before observing outcomes. Immutable master prompt reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Execution artifacts and deterministic analysis logs (execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, deterministic_reconciliation.json, and others) are archived in the registered evidence bundle and contain authoritative provider-call counts, model configuration, and validator traces. No human manual manuscript editing or content insertion occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Confirmatory ceiling/null outcome: baseline generator produced zero emulator faults on the preregistered task set, preventing direct measurement of verifier detection benefit under the shared_initial_candidate contract.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the design measures verifier effect on the same generated candidate only and does not assess independent per‑condition generation, multi‑sample generation, or repairs unless explicitly permitted by the contract.
Single‑model scope: experiments used one declared model (gpt-5-mini); results do not imply generality across models or versions.
Synthetic/emulated tasks: task corpus and emulator executions differ from production devices and live traffic; external validity to production deployments is limited.

Sampling‑parameter uncertainty: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null; null indicates provider default sampling semantics determined runtime sampling behavior and is recorded as residual uncertainty.

Residual contamination risk: deterministic provenance and exact‑match checks were applied, but private training‑data contamination of the hosted model cannot be fully ruled out and remains residual uncertainty.
